questions.q: What did the Israelites offer before God after the sacred chest was put in the middle of the tent that David had set up for it?
questions.a: They offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

questions.q: What did David distribute to every Israelite when he had finished blessing the people in the name of Yahweh?
questions.a: David distributed to each of them a loaf of bread, a date cake, and a raisin cake.

questions.q: What were the Levites appointed to do as they served in front of Yahweh’s sacred chest?
questions.a: They were appointed to thank and praise Yahweh, the God of Israel.

questions.q: What instruments did Asaph and the other Levites play?
questions.a: Asaph played the cymbals, and the other Levites played lyres and harps.

questions.q: Who played trumpets in front of the sacred chest?
questions.a: The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel played trumpets continually in front of the sacred chest of the covenant of God.

questions.q: What were Asaph and his brothers appointed to do?
questions.a: They were appointed to sing a song of thanksgiving to Yahweh.

questions.q: According to the song, what should people do among the other peoples?
questions.a: They should give thanks to Yahweh, call on his name, and make known his deeds among the peoples.

questions.q: What were people to speak about in the song that Asaph and his brothers sang?
questions.a: They were to speak of all of Yahweh’s marvelous deeds.

questions.q: Who were the people to boast about and seek?
questions.a: The people were to boast about and seek Yahweh.

questions.q: What are the descendants of Israel, Yahweh’s chosen ones, supposed to recall about Yahweh their God?
questions.a: They are to recall the marvelous things he has done, his miracles, and the decrees from his mouth.

questions.q: What did Yahweh make with Abraham that the Israelites are to keep in mind forever?
questions.a: He made a covenant with Abraham, and the Israelites are to keep Yahweh’s covenant in mind forever.

questions.q: What did Yahweh confirm to Jacob and to Israel?
questions.a: He confirmed it to Jacob as a statute, and to Israel as an everlasting covenant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh promise to give to his people as a share of their inheritance?
questions.a: Yahweh promised to give them the land of Canaan.

questions.q: How did Yahweh protect Israel when they were few in number and as they were going from one kingdom to another?
questions.a: He did not allow anyone to oppress them, and he rebuked kings because of them.

questions.q: What did Yahweh warn kings not to do to his people?
questions.a: He warned them not to touch his anointed ones or harm his prophets.

questions.q: What are the people to declare among the nations as they sing to Yahweh and announce his salvation day after day?
questions.a: They are to declare Yahweh’s glory and his marvelous deeds among all the nations.

questions.q: Who is it that has made the heavens and is to be praised greatly and feared above all other gods?
questions.a: It is Yahweh who made the heavens and is to be praised greatly and feared above all other gods.

questions.q: What does the song say is in Yahweh’s presence?
questions.a: Splendor and majesty are in his presence, and strength and joy are in his place.

questions.q: What is to be ascribed to Yahweh?
questions.a: Glory and strength are to be ascribed to Yahweh.

questions.q: What does the song tell people to bring to Yahweh, and how should they worship him?
questions.a: They should bring an offering to Yahweh and worship him in the splendor of his holiness.

questions.q: What does the song say about the world?
questions.a: The world is set firmly in place, and it will never be shaken.

questions.q: What will the nations say about Yahweh?
questions.a: The nations will say, “Yahweh reigns.”

questions.q: What does the song tell the sea and the fields to do?
questions.a: It tells the sea to roar and the fields to rejoice, along with everything in them.

questions.q: What are the trees in the forest going to do before Yahweh?
questions.a: The trees in the forest will shout for joy before him.

questions.q: What does the song say about Yahweh?
questions.a: It says that Yahweh is good and that his covenant faithfulness continues forever.

questions.q: Why should Yahweh gather his people together and rescue them from the other nations?
questions.a: He should gather them together and rescue them so that they may give thanks to his holy name and glory in his praises.

questions.q: For how long is Yahweh, the God of Israel to be praised?
questions.a: He is to be praised from everlasting to everlasting.

questions.q: What task did David give to Asaph and his brothers?
questions.a: David left them there to minister continually in front of the sacred chest of the covenant of Yahweh, doing each day what it required.

questions.q: Who did David appoint as gatekeepers?
questions.a: Obed Edom and his 68 brothers were gatekeepers, along with Obed Edom the son of Jeduthun and Hosah.

questions.q: Where did Zadok the priest and his fellow priests serve?
questions.a: They served in front of the tabernacle of Yahweh at the high place in Gibeon.

questions.q: Who commanded the Israelites to offer burnt offerings that way, and who wrote it down in the law?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded it, and Moses wrote it down in the law.

questions.q: Besides Asaph, who else did David choose by name to give thanks to Yahweh?
questions.a: He chose Heman and Jeduthun and the rest who were designated by name to give thanks to Yahweh, for his covenant faithfulness continues forever.

questions.q: What did Heman and Jeduthun do, and what did Jeduthun’s sons do?
questions.a: Heman and Jeduthun played trumpets, cymbals, and other musical instruments to praise God, and Jeduthun’s sons guarded the gate.

questions.q: After the celebration of placing the sacred chest, where did the people and David go?
questions.a: The people went to their own homes, and David returned to bless his own household.

commentary.text: The solemnity with which the ark was fixed.
Setting in order the worship of God.

Verses 1–6 Though God's word and ordinances may be clouded and eclipsed for a time, they shall shine out of obscurity. This was but a tent, a humble dwelling, yet this was the tabernacle which David, in his psalms, often speaks of with so much affection. David showed himself generous to his subjects, as he had found God gracious to him. Those whose hearts are enlarged with holy joy, should show it by being open-handed.

Let God be glorified in our praises. Let others be edified and taught, that strangers to him may be led to adore him. Let us ourselves triumph and trust in God. Those that give glory to God's name are allowed to glory in it. Let the everlasting covenant be the great matter of our joy his people of old, be remembered by us with thankfulness to him. Show forth from day to day his salvation, his promised salvation by Christ. We have reason to celebrate that from day to day; for we daily receive the benefit, and it is a subject that can never be exhausted. In the midst of praises, we must not forget to pray for the servants of God in distress.

The worship of God ought to be the work of every day. David put it into order. At Jerusalem, where the ark was, Asaph and his brethren were to minister before the ark continually, with songs of praise. No sacrifices were offered there, nor incense burnt, because the altars were not there; but David's prayers were directed as incense, and the lifting up of his hands as the evening sacrifice. So early did spiritual worship take place of ceremonial. Yet the ceremonial worship, being of Divine institution, must by no means be omitted; therefore at Gibeon, at the altars, the priests attended; for their work was to sacrifice and burn incense; and that they did continually, morning and evening, according to the law of Moses. As the ceremonies were types of the mediation of Christ, the observance of them was of great consequence. The attendance of his appointed ministers is right in itself, and encourages the people.
